g.text: COMMITMENT DECISION · WHEN THE MODEL FAVORS REDUCING
Alex's 19% threshold leaves little valuecushion on the extra $75m
Reducing annual growth from 20% to 19% removes $2.84m of value from the extra $75m,essentially eliminating its +$2.82m base-case value.
Marginal $75m inception NPV after the fee cut, $m
At 20% growth the extra $75m is worth+$2.82m; at 19% it is about zero(−$0.013m unrounded). The $2.84mdecline is far larger than the ~$0.66mmarginal benefit of the fee cut.
Positive IRR can still mean negative NPV
At 18% asset growth, LP IRR is 14.06%,below the assumed 15% discount rate.
All NPVs at model inception, discounted at 15%; scenarios are not forecasts or probability-weighted expected values.
At 10% growth either hurdle lifts the marginal NPV only to −$17.97m — still negative; better terms cannot rescue every weak case.

Source: Q6 OPERF decision!D42, D44, D45, D47 (equivalently Engine!L62, L70, L72, L77 × 75 ÷ 20,000); Engine!K70 for the 18% IRR; Engine!L71:L72 for the 19%point (interpolated break-even about 19.0045%); Sensitivity!C38. A negative downside scenario alone does not establish a negative expected NPV.
